# refactor(dx): replace Awilix with explicit factories and wire observers in composition

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Builds on the public application API: `src/app/api.ts` exists, no command or use case receives a
container, and `src/app/container.ts` is the only production file that imports Awilix. If
`src/app/api.ts` is missing, the base branch is too old; stop and say so.

## What

The application describes the capabilities it needs and never builds or looks up concrete
implementations itself. All construction and wiring happens at startup.

## Why

App currently assembles adapters and observers through a container. That hides what each operation
really needs and lets infrastructure creep into use cases.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases), `cli` (commands) and `composition`
(builds adapters, binds operations, starts the executable).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR, except that the construction decision below is final.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Decision: remove Awilix

Build adapters with explicit typed factories in `src/composition`, and keep the lifecycle wrappers in
`src/app/lifecycle.ts`. Do not build a registry, resolver or autowiring in its place. Copy this decision
and its reasons into the PR description.

A comparison of today's code, Awilix confined to composition, and explicit factories found:

- All three behave the same. The choice is about visible dependencies, not a bug being fixed.
- Production registers no Awilix disposers, so every container `dispose()` releases nothing. Cleanup is
  done by `withResource`, `releaseInOrder` and `releasingOnPanic`, which stay.
- A missing or mistyped dependency in a container factory's parameter compiles and fails at run time.
  With factories it is a compile error.
- With child scopes, marking `openSession` as a singleton compiles, and init then opens sandboxes with
  the old config and credentials.
- Overriding a registration after something has read it leaves part of the graph on the old value.
- Awilix disposal cannot follow jig's cleanup rules: it ignores a returned `Err` and reports failures by
  rejecting. The wrappers would be needed either way.

## Target

Spec sections: "Composition", "Application preparation and resource lifetime" (observers),
"Dependency lint", "Acceptance evidence" items 3, 5 and 8. The spec and several guides still call the
mechanism undecided; the decision above settles it.

- `src/app/container.ts` (22 adapter and observer imports) mixes adapter construction, scopes, lifecycle
  policy and execution preparation: `openRunRuntime`, `openSandboxRuntime`, `createAppContainer`,
  `runCapabilitiesOf`, the private `openRunScope`, `AppCradle` and `RunCradle`. Delete it.
- `src/app/sandbox-image.ts` (3 adapter imports: the image recipe, `readSandboxDockerfile` and `AGENTS`)
  and `src/app/observed-events.ts` (1 observer import) are app's other infrastructure imports.
- Composition gains the factories that implement `RunRuntime` and `SandboxRuntime` for the operations
  bound in `src/composition/main.ts`. Pass each factory only what it reads; do not make one shared bag
  of dependencies.
- App keeps the policy now in `openRunScope`: retrying a sandbox start with `transientRetryPolicy`,
  releasing a partial acquisition, and closing the session before disposing the scope. It works over
  lazy parts that composition supplies.
- These behaviors must hold afterwards. Each is covered once, in the spec of the module that owns it;
  keep the existing test where one already covers it, and add one only for a gap:
  - Building a runtime opens nothing. Status and an ended run open no sandbox, image or run log.
  - Two runs in one process share the console log, and keep their events, metrics and workspace apart.
  - Each `sandboxFor` uses the config and environment it was given, including its image name and
    credentials. It shares the runtime's log, and earlier sandboxes keep their own settings.
  - A start that may pass is retried and then opens, or returns its last failure. A configuration failure
    is not retried. Either failure leaves nothing open.
  - A panic while opening releases the scope. A panic while assembling it closes the session, then
    releases the scope. Both propagate as thrown.
  - Release order is session, scope, telemetry, run lock. A throwaway sandbox closes before its branch is
    removed. A cleanup failure replaces success and never replaces a work failure.
- App's lifecycle wrappers own lifecycle policy through supplied capabilities (lazy
  factories, scope capabilities). Domain, steps, flow and use cases never see a container,
  registration keys, resolution or scope APIs. Keep deferred construction where it matters, and
  avoid an application-wide dependency bag.
- Composition constructs concrete adapters and attaches observers (`src/observers/*`). App requests
  logs and events through ports only. Move the plain metrics/report data that app responses need
  into portable contracts, so app does not import observers.
- Keep custom run-store module loading: the adapter validates the module and its values, app picks
  required stores by policy, composition supplies the implementations.
- Observer isolation: an ordinary observer exception is reported and the other observers are still
  notified; a panic propagates.
- Shutdown flushes output after resources close.
- Lint: app cannot import `adapters`, `observers` or `cli`. Delete `awilixOnlyInApp` from
  `eslint.config.js` (two uses), and restrict Pino/OpenTelemetry to concrete reporting
  and wiring areas. Add fixtures.
- Specs that build the container: `src/app/container.spec.ts`, `src/app/run-jig.integration.spec.ts`
  (16 calls to `runCapabilitiesOf`, built through one `setup`) and
  `src/app/implement-issue.integration.spec.ts` (one `setup`). Move the
  behaviors `container.spec.ts` covers to specs beside their new owners, then delete it. Keep every
  assertion in the other two; only how they build the run changes. Specs need to replace the sandbox
  opener, images, log and retry settings (the fixed retry delay is 5 seconds).
- Remove the `awilix` dependency from `package.json` and the lockfile.
- Update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md` and
  `CLAUDE.md` (current picks), `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md`,
  `.claude/rules/testing-conventions.md`, and the statements in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`
  that call the mechanism undecided.

Out of scope: closing the run log file when its scope is released. It stays open until the process exits
today, and closing it is a behavior change. Keep the `dispose` contracts on `RunRuntime`,
`SandboxRuntime` and `RunScope`, even where production has nothing to release.

## Done when

- [ ] `grep -rnE "from '\.\./(adapters|observers)/" src/app --include='*.ts' --exclude='*.spec.ts'` finds
      nothing, and lint enforces it. Specs in `src/app` may keep importing adapters.
- [ ] `grep -rniE "awilix" src scripts package.json package-lock.json eslint.config.js` finds nothing.
- [ ] `grep -rnE "#49" src scripts .dependency-cruiser.mjs CONTRIBUTING.md .claude/rules docs/architecture.html docs/workflow-ownership.md docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`
      finds no text that calls the construction mechanism undecided.
- [ ] `src/app/lifecycle.spec.ts` and the "runJig over supplied capabilities" tests in
      `src/app/run-jig.spec.ts` pass unchanged, and every behavior listed under Target is
      covered once, by an existing spec or a new one.
- [ ] Observer failure isolation and panic propagation are tested.
- [ ] The built executable's `--help` and `github implement --help` work, and output is flushed after resources close.
- [ ] The full verification below passes, including `npm run validate`.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run validate
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.



Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/59

docs.design:
# Goal

Replace Awilix with explicit typed factories in `src/composition`, preserving application behavior and resource lifetimes. Remove all production app imports of adapters, observers and CLI without introducing a registry, resolver or shared application dependency bag.

# Context

The prerequisite `src/app/api.ts` exists. Commands already receive capability-based operations. `src/composition/main.ts` binds those operations and owns executable startup, but delegates runtime construction to `src/app/container.ts`.

Current ownership and required behavior map as follows:

| Behavior | Current owner and governing rules |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime construction, lazy run services and sandbox settings | `app/container.ts` constructs adapters, registers scoped logging/events/metrics, and creates separately configured sandboxes. The composition section of the specification requires construction to move out of app. |
| Sandbox retry and partial acquisition | Private `openRunScope` and `openSessionRetrying` in `app/container.ts`; `flow/retry-policy.ts` supplies `transientRetryPolicy`, config supplies resolved retry settings, and `failures/retry.ts` executes retries. |
| Cleanup ordering and failure precedence | `app/lifecycle.ts`, `app/report-cleanup.ts`, `app/run-jig.ts`, `app/run-operation.ts` and `app/throwaway-sandbox.ts`. The errors-as-values and callee-ownership rules require centralized lifetime wrappers, ordered release and preservation of work failures and panics. |
| Image preparation | `app/sandbox-image.ts` owns rebuild/update decisions but also imports recipe encoding, Dockerfile reading and provider metadata, calls Sandcastle naming, and reads host identity. This mixes application policy with infrastructure. |
| Observer attachment and isolation | `app/observed-events.ts` constructs `observers/RunEvents`; container wiring attaches logging, metrics and tracing observers. `observed-events.spec.ts` already covers ordinary exception isolation and panic propagation. |
| Portable application reports | `ports/run-records.ts` already owns `MetricsSummary` and document contracts. Reuse them rather than introducing duplicate types. |
| Store loading and selection | `adapters/run-store/repository-run-stores.ts` supplies and validates stores; app selects required stores. Preserve custom module loading and parsing at the edge. |
| Startup and output flushing | `composition/main.ts` awaits command parsing, then invokes `cli/exit-when-done.ts`. Application operations complete cleanup before returning. Imported builders and help must remain resource-free. |
| Boundary enforcement | `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`, `.dependency-cruiser.specs.mjs`, `scripts/lint-dependencies.integration.spec.ts` and ESLint. Current fixtures permit app construction, and ESLint restricts Awilix to app. |

`container.spec.ts` covers scope assembly, retry exhaustion, telemetry delivery, panic cleanup and sandbox configuration. The supplied-capabilities tests in `run-jig.spec.ts` already cover release order, cleanup precedence and ended runs. Both application integration suites construct containers in their setup helpers.

The house rules additionally require narrow typed inputs, no module mocking, adjacent behavior specs, one owner per tested rule, and no new source scanner. Architecture and ownership references must change with the code.

# Chosen approach

## Explicit construction with application-owned acquisition

Add focused composition factories for run runtimes, sandbox runtimes and run reporting. Bind them from `composition/main.ts`. Factories accept only inputs they read, using ordinary typed functions and objects. Concrete construction stays in composition or existing adapters; application modules receive portable capabilities.

Extract the policy currently in `openRunScope` into an app-owned acquisition module, provisionally `app/run-scope.ts`, using the existing wrappers in `app/lifecycle.ts`. Its supplied deferred parts expose only the operations needed to initialize reporting, open a session, assemble the session-dependent workspace and dispose the acquired scope. These are lifecycle capabilities, not container scopes: there are no registration keys, lookup methods or resolution APIs.

Establish disposal before running fallible deferred initialization. App then initializes reporting, retries session opening with `transientRetryPolicy`, and assembles the completed scope. A failed start disposes the partial scope and returns the last opening failure. A panic during opening disposes the scope; a panic after opening closes the session before disposal and propagates unchanged. Hand successful acquisition to the existing lifetime wrappers so release remains session, scope, telemetry and run lock, followed by runtime disposal at the operation boundary.

Keep `EngineDependencies` assembly in app. Composition supplies session, workspace, events and other portable inputs; app forms the workflow dependency object. This respects the existing prohibition on composition importing flow and avoids an exception merely to move the old container wholesale.

Retain `RunRuntime.dispose`, `SandboxRuntime.dispose` and `RunScope.dispose`, including explicit production no-ops. Production currently registers no Awilix disposers. Do not close run log files as part of this refactor.

## Deferred construction and isolation

Runtime construction does not open a sandbox, prepare an image or create a run log. Reporting and session-dependent resources are built only when app requests a run scope. Status and ended-run paths retain their existing short circuits.

Share the console logger within the composed runtime lifetime. Every run acquisition creates independent events, metrics and workspace state. Each `sandboxFor` call captures its own supplied configuration and environment, including image selection and credentials, while sharing the runtime logger. Later calls must not mutate earlier sandbox capabilities. Preserve deferred construction for image and session work.

Expose narrow typed factory inputs that integration setups can replace for sandbox opening, images, logging and resolved retry settings. Production keeps the existing five-second retry delay; tests can supply shorter settings without registration overrides or new operator configuration.

## Image and observer boundaries

Keep image rebuild decisions, update policy, configured-agent selection and warnings in `app/sandbox-image.ts`. Supply infrastructure through cohesive capabilities in `ports/sandbox-images.ts`: repository recipe preparation, portable installed-image metadata, provider package information, image naming and image construction. Adapters retain Dockerfile I/O, host UID/GID acquisition, label encoding/decoding, hashing, paths and Dockerfile generation. Prefer operations returning the information app needs over injecting each encoding constant or helper separately. Preserve managed-image bypass, build ordering and existing error messages.

Move `observed-events.ts` and its existing behavior coverage beside the composition wiring that owns observer attachment. Observers continue to own reporting behavior and event delivery mechanics. Ordinary observer exceptions are reported while delivery continues; panics propagate. If an existing case performs real file I/O, retain its assertions under the appropriate integration-spec classification.

Reuse `ports/run-records.ts` for response data and audit transitive application exports for concrete logger, telemetry, observer or adapter types. Keep store-module validation in adapters and store-selection policy in app.

## Enforcement and repository mismatches

Tighten Dependency Cruiser so production app cannot import adapters, observers or CLI through value imports, type imports, re-exports or literal dynamic imports. Preserve legitimate adapter imports in app specs and the existing public application entry restriction. Restrict Pino/OpenTelemetry imports to the concrete logging, telemetry, reporting and wiring modules that require them; portable consumers use ports.

The requested `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs` and its spec do not exist in this checkout. Extend the existing Dependency Cruiser configurations and `scripts/lint-dependencies.integration.spec.ts`; do not create another scanner.

The specification still defers the mechanism to #49. The request explicitly settles that decision, so replace those deferrals with explicit factories while retaining the specified ownership boundaries. Executable composition and portable report contracts already exist and need no duplicate implementation.

Record this decision and its reasons in the implementation PR: **Build adapters with explicit typed factories in `src/composition`, and keep lifecycle wrappers in `src/app/lifecycle.ts`. Do not replace Awilix with a registry, resolver or autowiring.** Equivalent behavior is required; visibility of dependencies motivates the change. Awilix has no registered production disposers; its factory dependency mistakes can compile; singleton child-scope state can retain obsolete settings and credentials; registration replacement can leave a mixed graph; and rejecting disposal cannot honor jig's Result-based cleanup semantics. Existing lifecycle wrappers remain necessary.

# Alternatives considered

1. **Retain current app-owned Awilix construction.** Rejected because app continues importing infrastructure and dependency resolution remains implicit. It violates the requested boundary and final construction decision.
2. **Move Awilix into composition.** This could satisfy source ownership, but retains runtime dependency errors, stale singleton/registration risks and disposal semantics incompatible with Result-based cleanup. It provides no production disposer benefit and contradicts the settled decision.
3. **Explicit factories with app-owned lifecycle policy — selected.** Typed dependencies become visible, lifetimes remain explicit and existing behavior is preserved. A wholesale move of lifecycle code into composition is excluded because composition must not own retry or cleanup policy.

# Assumptions

- Existing capability operations and runtime contracts remain the application boundary; this refactor does not redesign command APIs.
- Config/environment inputs are parsed at their existing edges and treated as captured values, not mutable shared registrations.
- Retry settings remain internal resolved settings; test injection introduces no public configuration option.
- Existing lifecycle and supplied-capabilities run tests remain unchanged. Other tests may change construction setup or move to their new owner while retaining behavior assertions.
- This is a design-only deliverable. No implementation files are created and validation results are not claimed.

# Non-goals

No new transport, plugin framework, generic scope manager, workflow engine, operator retry option or public behavior change. No run-log closure, new cleanup recovery, credential-independent status change or cleanup-warning policy change. No host agent execution, GitHub publication during validation, version bump or release tag.

Preserve sandbox-only unattended execution, credential secrecy and authorized init persistence, ignored scratch paths, target worktree isolation, dirty-tree merge protection, CLI output, configuration precedence and recovery behavior.

# Affected areas

- `src/composition/main.ts` and adjacent runtime/reporting factories and specs.
- `src/app/container.ts` and `container.spec.ts` removed after responsibilities and assertions migrate.
- App acquisition policy, image preparation and runtime capability types; existing lifecycle wrappers remain authoritative.
- `src/app/observed-events.ts` and its specs relocated to composition.
- Image ports/adapters and existing portable report contracts where necessary.
- `run-jig.integration.spec.ts` and `implement-issue.integration.spec.ts` setup helpers.
- Dependency Cruiser configurations, existing dependency fixtures, ESLint, `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.
- `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the callee-ownership and testing rules, `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`, and other existing references naming moved paths.

Confirm `src/app/api.ts` and inspect current runtime contracts, construction, image preparation, observers, startup and integration setup helpers. Read the applicable house rules and architecture map before edits.

Retain lifecycle cleanup precedence in `lifecycle.spec.ts`, run release order and ended-run behavior in the supplied-capabilities `run-jig.spec.ts` tests, throwaway closure ordering in its existing spec, and observer isolation in the moved observer-wiring spec. Identify gaps for retry success/non-retryable failure, lazy construction, repeated-run isolation, settings capture and shutdown ordering. Do not duplicate already-owned cases.

## Step 2 — Replace run construction while preserving acquisition policy

Introduce the narrow app-owned deferred acquisition contract and acquisition implementation, using `releasingOnPanic`, `withResource` and `releaseInOrder` rather than new lifecycle machinery. Keep retry classification and settings in their existing owners. Assemble `EngineDependencies` inside app from supplied portable parts.

Implement composition factories for run capabilities, reporting and session-dependent adapters. Wire run and GitHub implementation operations to them. Keep console logging shared, reporting lazy and each run's events, metrics and workspace independent. Preserve custom store loading through `RepositoryRunStores` and required-store selection in app.

Move container retry and panic-cleanup tests to the app acquisition owner; move concrete assembly and telemetry-wiring coverage to composition. Add only missing cases for successful retry, fatal failure without retry, partial acquisition release and repeated-run isolation. Preserve `lifecycle.spec.ts` and the supplied-capabilities run tests unchanged.

Replace container construction and registrations in both application integration setup helpers with typed factory inputs for session opening, images, log and retry settings. Keep every existing assertion and continue using fake sandbox sessions with real workflow logic. Run the affected unit and integration suites.

## Step 3 — Complete sandbox and image factory boundaries

Implement `SandboxRuntime` construction in composition with `sandboxFor` closures over each supplied configuration and environment. Share the runtime log without shared mutable settings. Preserve disposal contracts and lazy image/session work.

Split `app/sandbox-image.ts` by responsibility: app retains build/update decisions; ports describe portable recipe and image capabilities; adapters own Dockerfile reading, host identity, package metadata, naming and recipe serialization. Supply those implementations from composition and preserve image behavior for both runs and init/build operations.

Move the existing sandbox configuration test beside the composition factory and extend it only for uncovered image-name, environment/credential, logger-sharing and previous-settings retention cases. Keep image policy tests with app and infrastructure tests with adapters. Verify throwaway sandbox closure still precedes branch removal using its existing owning coverage.

## Step 4 — Finish reporting wiring and remove the container

Move observer attachment and `observed-events` into composition, carrying existing exception-isolation and panic-propagation assertions with it. Keep reporting behavior in observers and use `ports/run-records.ts` for application response data. Audit application contracts, including inferred and transitive types, for infrastructure leakage.

Finish replacing runtime imports in `composition/main.ts`; remove `app/container.ts`, its cradle types, registration helpers and obsolete spec after all behavior coverage has a new owner. Remove Awilix from `package.json` and the lockfile without changing the development version.

Verify runtime construction opens no sandbox, image or run log. Combine composition laziness coverage with the unchanged status/ended-run policy coverage rather than retesting those policies in composition.

## Step 5 — Enforce and document the completed boundaries

Update `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and the existing spec configuration so production app cannot import adapters, observers or CLI. Remove `awilixOnlyInApp` and both ESLint uses. Restrict Pino/OpenTelemetry to concrete reporting and wiring areas.
